statement: A Korean stock company (주식회사, chusik hoesa) comes into existence by registration of its incorporation at the seat of its principal office (Commercial Act Article 172). The incorporation registration must be made within two weeks from completion of the subscription and payment procedures for promoter-only incorporation, or from the close of the inaugural general meeting for subscription incorporation (Article 317(1)), and the registered particulars include the core articles items, the paid-in capital, the issued shares by class, the directors, and the representative director’s name and address (Article 317(2)).
caveat: Registrations are filed with the court registry (in practice through the Supreme Court’s Internet Registry Office, IROS) and carry registration licence tax under local tax law. The September 20, 2024 registry amendments trimmed the registered-matter mechanics, so older guides and the 2020-era KLRI translation differ in detail. Verify the live text before relying.
